data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Adjudication between rival criteria: the 'last complete event' criterion and the 'causal fingerprint' criterion are both necessary but neither is sufficient alone. The correct criterion is their conjunction: resumption is safe iff (1) the last event is well-formed and complete, AND (2) the causal fingerprint matches, AND (3) no intermediate event declares logical incompleteness (e.g., a 'begin' without a matching 'commit'). This conjunction subsumes both rivals and adds a logical-unit integrity check.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the system has no concept of multi-event logical units (every event is atomic and independent), criterion 3 is vacuous and the conjunction reduces to (1) AND (2).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the system uses deterministic replay from the last event, criterion 2 may be redundant because replay reconstructs the same causal identity from the log itself.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the reasoning envelope workflow explicitly permits multi-segment runs with explicit resume markers, criterion 3 is satisfied by the marker rather than by logical-unit completeness.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'last complete event' criterion ensures structural integrity of the log. The 'causal fingerprint' criterion ensures causal identity continuity. The 'logical-unit integrity' criterion ensures semantic coherence: multi-event units must be complete or explicitly aborted. Token-budget exhaustion can violate any of the three independently: mid-write (violates 1), model update (violates 2), mid-inference-step (violates 3). Since each violation independently corrupts a different aspect of identity, all three must hold. The mechanism is a three-stage gate: structural check, fingerprint check, logical-unit check.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
